newsitem.title: UK: Poland inflation seen in single digits in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Poland inflation seen in single digits in 1998.

text.p: Polish central bank chief Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said on Friday that the government should achieve its 13 percent inflation goal for 1997 and the rate may drop to single digits by 1998.
"We expect a further decline in the inflation rate," she told a conference in London."Maybe next year it will be a one digit number."
Gronkiewicz-Waltz forecast the 1997 rate at 13 percent, down from 17 percent at the end of 1996.
She also called for more privatisation measures. "We should privatise monopoly companies like telecommunications and insurance," she said.
The central bank governor said there was still some concern about the trade deficit and this could cause further problems in 1997.
"But if you compare the first quarter of 1996 with that of 1997, exports are increasing."
She said the growth in imports was quite normal considering Poland's need to import large amounts of high technology to bring its economy up to date. -- Brian Killen + 44 171 542 7715
